hero.intro: A cartridge valve screws into a machined cavity in a manifold block, so a whole circuit can live in one compact body with no pipework between the valves. Sun Hydraulics builds each function in frame sizes from series 0 to series 4; the series sets the cavity and the flow, and the configuration letters after the model code set the control, setting range, seals and material.

guidance.heading: Function first, then frame size and cavity
guidance.body: Pick the function — hold a load, limit pressure, meter flow, check or switch direction — then the flow you need, which fixes the series and the cavity. Send us the model code from the valve or the drawing, or the duty (flow, pressure, fluid and what the valve has to do), and we confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

hero.intro: Pressure-control cartridges limit or set pressure in a circuit. A relief valve caps system or line pressure; a reducing valve holds a lower pressure in a branch; a reducing/relieving valve also relieves back down to that setting; a sequence valve opens a second function only once the first has reached its pressure.

guidance.heading: Direct-acting or pilot-operated
guidance.body: Use a direct-acting valve to protect against over-pressure: it is very fast, tolerant of dirt and stable, and it is the safe choice when in doubt. Use a pilot-operated valve to regulate pressure: its pressure rises little as flow increases and it is easy to adjust. Then choose the setting range that covers your working setting and the capacity for the full flow the valve may have to pass.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics 2-Way, Direct-Acting Electro-Proportional, Pressure Compensated Flow Control Valve with Reverse Flow Check — FDEP
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics electro-proportional pressure-compensated flow control valve: FDEP, series 3, 30 gpm (120 L/min), T-16A cavity. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A normally closed flow control whose flow is set by a proportional solenoid and held steady by an integral compensator, from nearly closed to full flow. A high-capacity check passes return flow freely from port 2 to port 1.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 1 size. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FDEP — series 3, T-16A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Typical response time: 50 ms

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for FDEP; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: X — No Manual Override
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Option rules: If the coil is in this group (211, 212, 212D, 212X01, 212X02, 214, 214D, 214L, 214X01, 214X02, 223, 224, 224D, 224X01, 224X02, 228, 228D, 228X01, 228X02, 612, 612D, 614, 614D, 624, 624D, 628, 628D, 712, 712D, 714, 714D, 724, 724D, 728, 728D, 812, 812D, 814, 814D, 824, 824D, 828, 828D, 912, 912D, 912X01, 912X02, 914, 914D, 914X01, 914X02, 924, 924D, 924X01, 924X02, 928, 928D, 928X01, 928X02, JM11BD, JM11CD, JM12BD, JM12CD, JM23BD, JM23CD, JM24BD, JM24CD, JN11BD, JN11CD, JN12BD, JN12CD, JN23BD, JN23CD, JN24BD, JN24CD), the range must be C, A or B.

Selection notes

  • Zinc-nickel plating as standard.
  • Coil connector options up to IP69K.

Where it is used

Electronically controlled speeds under changing load — lifts, winches, conveyors and fans.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm); installation torque 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 3: Buna: 990016007, Viton: 990016006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example FDEPXBN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

faqs.question: What do I need to drive it?
faqs.answer: A proportional amplifier with current control and adjustable dither, matched to the coil. Sun's XMD drivers are configured for its coils; the coil voltage and connector are ordering options.

faqs.question: What does pressure compensated mean?
faqs.answer: The valve holds its flow steady while the load or supply pressure changes, so an actuator keeps its speed. A needle valve does not: its flow changes with the square root of the pressure drop across it.

faqs.question: What does the full Sun model code mean?
faqs.answer: The four letters are the base model: valve type, frame size and variant. The letters that follow choose the control, setting range, seal material and any material or coating option. We confirm the full code, for example FDEPXBN, with the quotation.

faqs.question: How do I order or get a quotation?

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?
faqs.answer: Only the external seals. Sun supplies a seal kit for every cartridge, and the kit numbers for this valve are listed under Installation and seal kits. Fitting a different external seal material does not make the valve compatible with a new fluid, because the internal seals stay as built.

faqs.question: How is the cartridge installed?
faqs.answer: It screws into a cavity machined to Sun's drawing for its series, and is tightened to the installation torque given in the specifications. Valves with an integral T-8A pilot cavity go in first, and the pilot cartridge is then fitted into them to its own torque.

products.descriptionLong:
A 2-way, 2-position throttle opened by pilot pressure: pressure at port 1 opens a metering orifice between ports 2 and 3 in proportion to it, while pressure at port 4 works against it. The balance of spring, flow and pilot forces gives partial self-compensation as load changes. Bleed-down versions connect port 3 to port 4 when closed, and dual-path versions double the flow area.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 4 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FTCA — series 2, T-52AD cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • FTDA — series 2, T-52AD cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)
  • FTEA — series 3, T-53AD cavity, 25 gpm (95 L/min)
  • FTFA — series 3, T-53AD cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 5 in³/min.@1000 psi (80 cc/min.@70 bar), 10 in³/min.@1000 psi (160 cc/min.@70 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for FTFA; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: L — Stroke Adjustment, X — Not Adjustable
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated, /LH — Mild Steel, Zinc-Nickel

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be X.

Selection notes

  • Can be fully pressure compensated by adding an external modulating element.
  • An optional tuning control varies the pilot pressure needed for a given flow.

Where it is used

Joystick-piloted speed control on mobile machines, and meter-in control ahead of counterbalance valves (bleed-down versions).

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm); installation torque 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 2: Buna: 990152007, Viton: 990152006; series 3: Buna: 990053007, Viton: 990053006.

A sliding-spool, pressure-compensated valve that divides flow in one direction and combines it in the other, so two cylinders or motors can be run together both ways. faqs.question: Will a flow divider keep two cylinders exactly in step?
faqs.answer: No valve can truly synchronise two cylinders. The divider holds its published accuracy, but the error does not average out: the higher-pressure leg gains on every stroke. Synchronising divider/combiners correct the error at the end of each stroke, once the leading cylinder bottoms out; cross-port reliefs are another way.

faqs.question: What happens when one side carries more load?
faqs.answer: When dividing, the more heavily loaded leg takes slightly more of the flow. If the actuators are tied together rigidly, the leading one can drag the other and make it cavitate.

faqs.question: How is a fixed-orifice valve ordered?
faqs.answer: You state the flow you need and it is set at the factory, within about ±15% (±10% on some ventable types). A tuneable control option lets you trim it by about ±20% in the field.

faqs.question: What does pressure compensated mean?
faqs.answer: The valve holds its flow steady while the load or supply pressure changes, so an actuator keeps its speed. A needle valve does not: its flow changes with the square root of the pressure drop across it.

faqs.question: Will it fit my existing flow-control cavity?
faqs.answer: Sun's 2-port flow-control cartridges of one frame size share the same cavity and flow path, so they interchange; only the height they stand above the manifold can differ.

faqs.question: What does the full Sun model code mean?
faqs.answer: The four letters are the base model: valve type, frame size and variant. The letters that follow choose the control, setting range, seal material and any material or coating option. We confirm the full code, for example FXCCXAN, with the quotation.

faqs.question: How do I order or get a quotation?
faqs.answer: Send us the Sun model code — from the valve itself or the machine drawing — with the quantity, or describe the duty if you are choosing a new valve. We confirm the full ordering code, price and delivery with the quotation. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?
faqs.answer: Only the external seals. Sun supplies a seal kit for every cartridge, and the kit numbers for this valve are listed under Installation and seal kits. Fitting a different external seal material does not make the valve compatible with a new fluid, because the internal seals stay as built.

The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

  • Typical response time: 50 ms

Electronically set priority and fan-drive circuits on mobile machines.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics FLeX Series Pilot-Operated, Normally Closed, Electro-Proportional Throttle, Flow 2-1 — FPBF
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics pilot-operated electro-proportional throttle: FPBF, series 0, 5 gpm (20 L/min), T-162A cavity. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated proportional throttle with a poppet main stage: the coil acts on a small pilot that opens or closes the main poppet in proportion to current. Normally closed and normally open versions exist, with or without a free-flow reverse check; FLeX Series models are built for XMD drivers.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 1 size. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FPBF — series 0, T-162A cavity, 5 gpm (20 L/min), 0-series

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 0.004 in³/min.@3000 psi (0,07 cc/min.@210 bar)
  • Typical response time: 50 ms
  • Check cracking pressure: 100 psi (7 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for FPBF; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: X — No Manual Override
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton

Option rules: If the coil is in this group (212, 212D, 212X01, 212X02, 214, 214D, 214X01, 214X02, 224, 224D, 224X01, 224X02, 228, 228D, 228X01, 228X02, 612, 612D, 614, 614D, 624, 624D, 628, 628D, 712, 712D, 714, 714D, 724, 724D, 728, 728D, 812, 812D, 814, 814D, 824, 824D, 828, 828D, 912, 912D, 912X01, 912X02, 914, 914D, 914X01, 914X02, 924, 924D, 924X01, 924X02, 928, 928D, 928X01, 928X02, JM24BD, JM24CD, JN24BD, JN24CD), the range must be D.

Selection notes

  • Very low leakage in the closed position.
  • Without the check, reverse flow closes the valve and only pilot flow passes.
  • FLeX Series versions are cycle-tested to 10 million operations.

Where it is used

Leak-tight proportional control of mobile functions — lowering, slewing and lift circuits.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 3/4 in. (19,1 mm); installation torque 20 - 25 lbf ft (27 - 33 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 0: Buna: 990162007, Viton: 990162006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example FPBFXDN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?
faqs.answer: Only the external seals. Sun supplies a seal kit for every cartridge, and the kit numbers for this valve are listed under Installation and seal kits. Fitting a different external seal material does not make the valve compatible with a new fluid, because the internal seals stay as built.

faqs.answer: It screws into a cavity machined to Sun's drawing for its series, and is tightened to the installation torque given in the specifications. Valves with an integral T-8A pilot cavity go in first, and the pilot cartridge is then fitted into them to its own torque.

faqs.question: Will a flow divider keep two cylinders exactly in step?
faqs.answer: No valve can truly synchronise two cylinders. The divider holds its published accuracy, but the error does not average out: the higher-pressure leg gains on every stroke. Synchronising divider/combiners correct the error at the end of each stroke, once the leading cylinder bottoms out; cross-port reliefs are another way.

faqs.question: What happens when one side carries more load?
faqs.answer: When dividing, the more heavily loaded leg takes slightly more of the flow. If the actuators are tied together rigidly, the leading one can drag the other and make it cavitate.

faqs.question: What does pressure compensated mean?
faqs.answer: The valve holds its flow steady while the load or supply pressure changes, so an actuator keeps its speed. A needle valve does not: its flow changes with the square root of the pressure drop across it.

  • NFFC — series 4, T-18A cavity, 60 gpm (.56 inch) (240 L/min. (14,2 mm))

A sliding-spool, pressure-compensated valve that divides flow in one direction and combines it in the other, so two cylinders or motors can be run together both ways. Closed-centre designs block the outlets from each other at rest; high-accuracy versions hold the split more closely; high-capacity versions carry about 15% more flow for traction drives, with lower accuracy.

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 5 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FSBA — series 1, T-31A cavity, .6 - 3 gpm (2,5 - 12 L/min)
  • FSDG — series 2, T-32A cavity, 1.5 - 8 gpm (6 - 30 L/min)
  • FSEG — series 3, T-33A cavity, 3 - 15 gpm (12 - 60 L/min)
  • FSFG — series 4, T-34A cavity, 6 - 30 gpm (23 - 120 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

faqs.question: Will a flow divider keep two cylinders exactly in step?
faqs.answer: No valve can truly synchronise two cylinders. The divider holds its published accuracy, but the error does not average out: the higher-pressure leg gains on every stroke. Synchronising divider/combiners correct the error at the end of each stroke, once the leading cylinder bottoms out; cross-port reliefs are another way.

faqs.question: What happens when one side carries more load?
faqs.answer: When dividing, the more heavily loaded leg takes slightly more of the flow. If the actuators are tied together rigidly, the leading one can drag the other and make it cavitate.

faqs.question: Will a flow divider keep two cylinders exactly in step?
faqs.answer: No valve can truly synchronise two cylinders. The divider holds its published accuracy, but the error does not average out: the higher-pressure leg gains on every stroke. Synchronising divider/combiners correct the error at the end of each stroke, once the leading cylinder bottoms out; cross-port reliefs are another way.

faqs.question: What happens when one side carries more load?
faqs.answer: When dividing, the more heavily loaded leg takes slightly more of the flow. If the actuators are tied together rigidly, the leading one can drag the other and make it cavitate.

faqs.question: What does the full Sun model code mean?
faqs.answer: The four letters are the base model: valve type, frame size and variant. The letters that follow choose the control, setting range, seal material and any material or coating option. We confirm the full code, for example LRDSXHN, with the quotation.

faqs.question: How do I order or get a quotation?
faqs.answer: Send us the Sun model code — from the valve itself or the machine drawing — with the quantity, or describe the duty if you are choosing a new valve. We confirm the full ordering code, price and delivery with the quotation. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?
faqs.answer: Only the external seals. Sun supplies a seal kit for every cartridge, and the kit numbers for this valve are listed under Installation and seal kits. Fitting a different external seal material does not make the valve compatible with a new fluid, because the internal seals stay as built.

faqs.question: How is the cartridge installed?
faqs.answer: It screws into a cavity machined to Sun's drawing for its series, and is tightened to the installation torque given in the specifications. Valves with an integral T-8A pilot cavity go in first, and the pilot cartridge is then fitted into them to its own torque.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics Normally Open, Bi-Directional, Modulating Element — LHDT, LHFT, LHHT, Series 1 to 3
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics normally open modulating element: LHDT, LHFT, LHHT, series 1 to 3, 15 gpm to 60 gpm (60 L/min to 240 L/min), T-31A, T-32A, T-33A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A normally open modulating element that acts as a restrictive compensator: with an external orifice it holds a constant pressure drop across it so flow stays steady as pressure changes. The bi-directional version compensates in both directions.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 3 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • LHDT — series 1, T-31A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • LHFT — series 2, T-32A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)
  • LHHT — series 3, T-33A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for LHDT; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: X — Not Adjustable
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Option rules: If the seal is E, the control must be X.

Selection notes

  • A tuning control trims the pressure drop, and so the flow, by about ±25%.

Where it is used

Restrictive pressure-compensated flow controls built into a manifold.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 7/8 in. (22,2 mm), 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 1: Buna: 990031007, EPDM: 990031014, Polyurethane: 990031002, Viton: 990031006; series 2: Buna: 990032007, EPDM: 990032014, Polyurethane: 990032002, Viton: 990032006; series 3: Buna: 990033007, EPDM: 990033014, Polyurethane: 990033002, Viton: 990033006.

products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics pilot-operated electro-proportional throttle: FPFK, FPHK, series 2 to 3, 20 gpm to 60 gpm (80 L/min to 240 L/min), T-5A, T-16A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated proportional throttle with a poppet main stage: the coil acts on a small pilot that opens or closes the main poppet in proportion to current. Normally closed and normally open versions exist, with or without a free-flow reverse check; FLeX Series models are built for XMD drivers.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 2 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FPFK — series 2, T-5A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min)
  • FPHK — series 3, T-16A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum leakage: 20 drops/min.@5000 psi

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for FPHK; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: X — No Manual Override, E — Twist (Extended) Manual Override, M — Manual Override
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, L — Extended Temp. Buna, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Option rules: If the coil is in this group (HN24AA, HN24AB), the control must be M or X; If the seal is E, the control must be E,M or X.

Selection notes

  • Very low leakage in the closed position.
  • Without the check, reverse flow closes the valve and only pilot flow passes.

faqs.question: Will a flow divider keep two cylinders exactly in step?
faqs.answer: No valve can truly synchronise two cylinders. The divider holds its published accuracy, but the error does not average out: the higher-pressure leg gains on every stroke. Synchronising divider/combiners correct the error at the end of each stroke, once the leading cylinder bottoms out; cross-port reliefs are another way.

faqs.question: What happens when one side carries more load?
faqs.answer: When dividing, the more heavily loaded leg takes slightly more of the flow. If the actuators are tied together rigidly, the leading one can drag the other and make it cavitate.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 4 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • FVFA8 — series 4, T-24A cavity, 50 gpm (200 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton

Selection notes

  • Factory-set priority flow, within about ±10%.

products.title: Sun Hydraulics Air-Controlled, Pilot-Operated, Pressure Reducing/Relieving Valve — PPFC, PPHC, PPJC, Series 2 to 4
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics air-controlled pressure reducing/relieving valve, 20:1 pilot ratio: PPFC, PPHC, PPJC, series 2 to 4, 20 gpm to 80 gpm (80 L/min to 320 L/min), T-2A, T-17A, T-19A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated reducing/relieving cartridge set by compressed air on a diaphragm. The reduced hydraulic pressure at port 1 follows the air pressure at 20:1, and port 1 is relieved to tank at full flow if driven above it.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 3 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • PPFC — series 2, T-2A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min)
  • PPHC — series 3, T-17A cavity, 40 gpm (160 L/min)
  • PPJC — series 4, T-19A cavity, 80 gpm (320 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Pilot ratio: 20:1
  • Maximum operating pressure: 2000 psi (140 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for PPJC; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: B — External 4-SAE Port
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton

Selection notes

  • Maximum operating pressure is lower than spring-set valves — check the rating.
  • Hydraulic setting = 20 × air pressure.

Where it is used

Pneumatically set clamping, tension and press circuits.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 2: Buna: 990202007, Polyurethane: 990002002, Viton: 990202006; series 3: Buna: 990017007, Polyurethane: 990017002, Viton: 990017006; series 4: Buna: 990019007, Polyurethane: 990019002, Viton: 990019006.

Ordering

Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example PPJCBBN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

faqs.answer: On the 3-port versions, yes: pressure at port 3 adds one-for-one to the setting, and Sun limits it to 3,000 psi (210 bar). Versions with a drain at port 4 are not affected by it.

faqs.question: Reducing valve or reducing/relieving valve — what is the difference?
faqs.answer: Both hold a lower, steady pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2. A plain reducing valve only closes off: if something pushes the reduced side above the setting, or the reduced circuit is dead-ended with very little leakage, the pressure can creep up. A reducing/relieving valve also opens port 1 to tank (port 3) to hold the setting.

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?

products.focusKeyword: direct-acting reducing/relieving valve with open transition
products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics direct-acting reducing/relieving valve with open transition: PRBC, PRDC, series 0 to 1, 5 gpm to 10 gpm (20 L/min to 40 L/min), T-163A, T-11A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A direct-acting reducing/relieving cartridge that stays slightly open as it moves from reducing to relieving. That gives tighter pressure control and quicker response, in exchange for a small, steady flow to tank.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 2 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • PRBC — series 0, T-163A cavity, 5 gpm (20 L/min), 0-series
  • PRDC — series 1, T-11A cavity, 10 gpm (40 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 20 in³/min. (330 cc/min)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for PRDC; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, K — Handknob, L — Standard Screw Adjustment, O — Handknob with Panel Mount
  • Setting range: A — 500 - 3000 psi (35 - 210 bar), 700 psi (50 bar) Standard Setting, B — 50 - 1500 psi (3,5 - 105 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, D — 25 - 800 psi (1,7 - 55 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, E — 25 - 400 psi (1,7 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, S — 25 - 200 psi (1,7 - 14 bar), 100 psi (7 bar) Standard Setting, W — 750 - 4500 psi (50 - 315 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the seal is E, the control must be C,K,L or O.

Selection notes

  • Leakage out of port 3 is higher by design; it rises with pressure difference.
  • Pressure at port 3 adds one-for-one to the setting; keep it under 3,000 psi (210 bar).

Where it is used

Pressure control where dynamic response matters more than leakage — pilot supplies and proportional circuits.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 3/4 in. (19,1 mm), 7/8 in. (22,2 mm); installation torque 20 - 25 lbf ft (27 - 33 Nm), 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 0: Buna: 990163007, Viton: 990163006; series 1: Buna: 990011007, EPDM: 990011014, Polyurethane: 990011002, Viton: 990011006.

Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example PRDCLAN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

  • SCGA — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)
  • SCIA — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 10 drops/min. (0,7 cc/min)
  • Typical response time: 2 ms
  • Check cracking pressure: 40 psi (2,8 bar), 25 psi (1,7 bar)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for SCCA; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: L — Standard Screw Adjustment, C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, K — Handknob
  • Setting range: A — 500 - 3000 psi (35 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, W — 800 - 4500 psi (55 - 315 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, B — 300 - 1500 psi (20 - 105 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, C — 2000 - 6000 psi (140 - 420 bar), 2000 psi (140 bar) Standard Setting, D — 200 - 800 psi (14 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, E — 100 - 400 psi (7 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, L — Extended Temp. Buna, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Option rules: EPDM seals are not allowed on modifier /LH; If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be C or L; If the seal is E, the control must be C,K or L.

Selection notes

  • Pressure at port 3 adds one-for-one to the setting.

products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics electro-proportional reducing/relieving valve: PRDP, series 1, 5 gpm (20 L/min), T-11A cavity. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A direct-acting reducing/relieving cartridge set by a proportional solenoid. The coil current sets the reduced pressure at port 1; if port 1 rises above it, the valve relieves to tank at port 3. Most versions are closed in the transition between reducing and relieving, so they use very little oil.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 1 size. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • PRDP — series 1, T-11A cavity, 5 gpm (20 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 2.5 in³/min. (41 cc/min)

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for PRDP; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: M — Manual Override (Standard), E — Twist (Extended) Manual Override, L — Standard Screw Adjustment, X — No Manual Override
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM

Option rules: If the coil is in this group (HN24AA, HN24AB), the control must be M or X; If the seal is E, the control must be E,L,M or X.

Selection notes

  • Standard versions rise with current; 'high setting with no command' versions fall with current.
  • Variants add a port-4 drain, an open transition or 740-Series coils; the coil is an ordering option.
  • Use a driver with current control and dither.

Where it is used

Electronic pilot-pressure control of mobile and industrial valves, clutches, brakes and pump displacement.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 7/8 in. (22,2 mm); installation torque 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 1: Buna: 990511007, Viton: 990511006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example PRDPMDN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

products.descriptionShort: Sun Hydraulics pilot-operated sequence valve: RSBC, RSDC, RSFC, RSHC, RSJC, series 0 to 4, 7.5 gpm to 120 gpm (30 L/min to 480 L/min), T-163A, T-11A, T-2A, T-17A, T-19A cavities. Authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor, UAE — supplied direct from Sun.
products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated sequence cartridge, with a balanced piston or balanced poppet main stage, opens the secondary branch once inlet pressure passes the setting (measured against the drain at port 3). It ignores back-pressure at its outlet up to the setting.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 5 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • RSBC — series 0, T-163A cavity, 7.5 gpm (30 L/min), 0-series
  • RSDC — series 1, T-11A cavity, 15 gpm (60 L/min)
  • RSFC — series 2, T-2A cavity, 30 gpm (120 L/min)
  • RSHC — series 3, T-17A cavity, 60 gpm (240 L/min)
  • RSJC — series 4, T-19A cavity, 120 gpm (480 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Ratings

  • Maximum operating pressure: 5000 psi (350 bar)
  • Maximum leakage: 2 in³/min. (30 cc/min), 2 in³/min.@1000 psi (30 cc/min.@70 bar), 3 in³/min.@1000 psi (50 cc/min.@70 bar), 4 in³/min.@1000 psi (65 cc/min.@70 bar), 5 in³/min.@1000 psi (80 cc/min.@70 bar)
  • Typical response time: 10 ms

Configuration options

The letters after the base model code choose these options (shown for RSDC; a size may add or drop a choice):

  • Control: L — Standard Screw Adjustment, C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, J — Capped Screw Adjustment, K — Handknob, O — Handknob with Panel Mount, W — Hex Wrench Adjustment, Y — Tri-Grip Handknob, F — Hex Head Screw with Locknut, M — Capped Screw Adjustment with Lockwire Holes, Q — Capped and Lockwired
  • Setting range: A — 100 - 3000 psi (7 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, W — 150 - 4500 psi (10,5 - 315 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, B — 50 - 1500 psi (3,5 - 105 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, C — 150 - 6000 psi (10,5 - 420 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, D — 25 - 800 psi (1,7 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, E — 25 - 400 psi (1,7 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, N — 60 - 800 psi (4 - 55 bar), 400 psi (28 bar) Standard Setting, Q — 60 - 400 psi (4 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, G — 60 - 3000 psi (4 - 210 bar), 1000 psi (70 bar) Standard Setting, P — 40 - 400 psi (2,8 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting
  • Seal material: N — Buna-N, V — Viton, E — EPDM
  • Material / coating: /AP — Stainless Steel, Passivated, /LH — Mild Steel, Zinc-Nickel

Option rules: If the modifier is /AP, the control must be C or L; If the modifier is /LH, the control must be L; If the seal is E, the control must be C,K,L,O or Y.

Selection notes

  • Pilot flow rises as inlet pressure climbs above the setting.
  • Balanced-poppet versions modulate inside the cartridge, limiting cavitation noise and erosion.

Where it is used

Sequencing on high-flow circuits, and pressure regulation where the return line is pressurised.

Installation and seal kits

Valve hex 3/4 in. (19,1 mm), 7/8 in. (22,2 mm), 1 1/8 in. (28,6 mm), 1 1/4 in. (31,8 mm), 1 5/8 in. (41,3 mm); installation torque 20 - 25 lbf ft (27 - 33 Nm), 30 - 35 lbf ft (41 - 47 Nm), 45 - 50 lbf ft (61 - 68 Nm), 150 - 160 lbf ft (203 - 217 Nm), 350 - 375 lbf ft (474 - 508 Nm). Replacement seal kits — series 0: Buna: 990163007, Polyurethane: 990163002, Viton: 990163006; series 1: Buna: 990011007, EPDM: 990011014, Polyurethane: 990011002, Viton: 990011006; series 2: Buna: 990202007, EPDM: 990202014, Polyurethane: 990002002, Viton: 990202006; series 3: Buna: 990017007, Polyurethane: 990017002, Viton: 990017006; series 4: Buna: 990019007, Polyurethane: 990019002, Viton: 990019006.

Ordering

Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE and supplies the range direct from Sun Hydraulics. Quote the base model and its configuration letters — for example RSDCLAN — or send us the flow, pressure and duty and we select the valve. We confirm the full ordering code with the quotation.

faqs.question: Reducing valve or reducing/relieving valve — what is the difference?
faqs.answer: Both hold a lower, steady pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2. A plain reducing valve only closes off: if something pushes the reduced side above the setting, or the reduced circuit is dead-ended with very little leakage, the pressure can creep up. A reducing/relieving valve also opens port 1 to tank (port 3) to hold the setting.

faqs.question: Can oil flow back from the reduced side to the supply?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A full reverse flow from port 1 to port 2 can shut the main spool, so add a separate check valve where the circuit needs free reverse flow.

faqs.question: Do reducing and reducing/relieving cartridges share a cavity?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sun's 3-port reducing and reducing/relieving cartridges of one frame size use the same cavity and flow path, so one can replace the other.

faqs.question: Reducing valve or reducing/relieving valve — what is the difference?
faqs.answer: Both hold a lower, steady pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2. A plain reducing valve only closes off: if something pushes the reduced side above the setting, or the reduced circuit is dead-ended with very little leakage, the pressure can creep up. A reducing/relieving valve also opens port 1 to tank (port 3) to hold the setting.

faqs.question: Can oil flow back from the reduced side to the supply?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A full reverse flow from port 1 to port 2 can shut the main spool, so add a separate check valve where the circuit needs free reverse flow.

faqs.question: Do reducing and reducing/relieving cartridges share a cavity?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sun's 3-port reducing and reducing/relieving cartridges of one frame size use the same cavity and flow path, so one can replace the other.

The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Configuration options

faqs.question: Reducing valve or reducing/relieving valve — what is the difference?
faqs.answer: Both hold a lower, steady pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2. A plain reducing valve only closes off: if something pushes the reduced side above the setting, or the reduced circuit is dead-ended with very little leakage, the pressure can creep up. A reducing/relieving valve also opens port 1 to tank (port 3) to hold the setting.

faqs.question: Can oil flow back from the reduced side to the supply?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A full reverse flow from port 1 to port 2 can shut the main spool, so add a separate check valve where the circuit needs free reverse flow.

products.descriptionLong:
A pilot-operated reducing/relieving cartridge holds a constant reduced pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2 and relieves port 1 to tank (port 3) at full flow if it is pushed above the setting. The pilot stage gives a flat pressure curve and very little dead band between reducing and relieving.

Sizes and cavities

Sun Hydraulics builds this valve in 4 sizes. The series sets the cavity it screws into and its flow capacity:

  • PPDF — series 1, T-11A cavity, 10 gpm (40 L/min)
  • PPFF — series 2, T-2A cavity, 20 gpm (80 L/min)
  • PPHF — series 3, T-17A cavity, 40 gpm (160 L/min)
  • PPJF — series 4, T-19A cavity, 80 gpm (320 L/min)

Sun builds its cartridges in frame sizes called series, from the small series 0 to series 4. The series fixes the cavity the valve screws into, so every function in one series shares that cavity, and a larger series carries more flow. Choose the smallest series that passes your flow at an acceptable pressure drop, using the performance curves, then the configuration options for control, setting and seals. If you are replacing a valve, the model code stamped on it gives the series and function directly, and the seal kits listed further down fit that series.

Configuration options

  • Control: C — Tamper Resistant - Factory Set, K — Handknob, L — Standard Screw Adjustment, Y — Tri-Grip Handknob, O — Handknob with Panel Mount, Q — Capped and Lockwired
  • Setting range: A — 100 - 3000 psi (7 - 210 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, B — 50 - 1500 psi (3,5 - 105 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, N — 60 - 800 psi (4 - 55 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, Q — 60 - 400 psi (4 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, W — 150 - 4500 psi (10,5 - 315 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, C — 150 - 6000 psi (10,5 - 420 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, D — 25 - 800 psi (1,7 - 55 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, E — 25 - 400 psi (1,7 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, H — 30 - 3000 psi (2 - 210 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, J — 25 - 1500 psi (1,7 - 105 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, K — 75 - 1500 psi (5 - 105 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, O — 150 - 400 psi (10 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting, P — 40 - 400 psi (2,8 - 28 bar), 200 psi (14 bar) Standard Setting

faqs.question: Reducing valve or reducing/relieving valve — what is the difference?
faqs.answer: Both hold a lower, steady pressure at port 1 from a higher supply at port 2. A plain reducing valve only closes off: if something pushes the reduced side above the setting, or the reduced circuit is dead-ended with very little leakage, the pressure can creep up. A reducing/relieving valve also opens port 1 to tank (port 3) to hold the setting.

faqs.question: Can oil flow back from the reduced side to the supply?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. A full reverse flow from port 1 to port 2 can shut the main spool, so add a separate check valve where the circuit needs free reverse flow.

faqs.question: Does pressure in the tank line change the setting?
faqs.answer: On the 3-port versions, yes: pressure at port 3 adds one-for-one to the setting, and Sun limits it to 3,000 psi (210 bar). Versions with a drain at port 4 are not affected by it.

faqs.question: What does the full Sun model code mean?
faqs.answer: The four letters are the base model: valve type, frame size and variant. The letters that follow choose the control, setting range, seal material and any material or coating option. We confirm the full code, for example PPDFLAN, with the quotation.

faqs.question: How do I order or get a quotation?
faqs.answer: Send us the Sun model code — from the valve itself or the machine drawing — with the quantity, or describe the duty if you are choosing a new valve. We confirm the full ordering code, price and delivery with the quotation. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised Sun Hydraulics distributor in the UAE.

faqs.question: Which parts of the cartridge can be serviced?
faqs.answer: Only the external seals. Sun supplies a seal kit for every cartridge, and the kit numbers for this valve are listed under Installation and seal kits. Fitting a different external seal material does not make the valve compatible with a new fluid, because the internal seals stay as built.
